name: Spirit Elk
body:
Spirit Elk
CR 18

This massive elk is covered in white, matted fur. Its majestic, thick antlers span 15 feet but the head they grace is terrifying. Blue, glowing eyes above a smiling grimace of sharp teeth.

XP 153,600
NE Large magical beast (cold)
Init +7; Senses darkvision 120 ft., low-light vision, true seeing; Perception +30

Aura cold (10 ft., 3d6 cold damage)

DEFENSE

AC 31, touch 17, flat-footed 23 (+7 Dex, +1 dodge, +14 natural, –1 size)
hp 290 (20d10+180); fast healing 30
Fort +21, Ref +19, Will +13
Defensive Abilities freedom of movement, rejuvenation;
DR 20/cold iron and magic; Immune cold, disease, fatigue, poison; SR 29
Weaknesses Vulnerability to fire

OFFENSE

Speed 60 ft.; air walk
Melee gore +32 (4d6+24/19-20/x3), bite +31 (2d6+12), 2 hooves +26 (1d8+6)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks devastating antlers, spirit walk, powerful charge (8d6+48), trample (4d6+18, DC 32)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 20th; concentration +26)

Constant—air walk, freedom of movement, true seeing
At will—cone of cold (DC 21), dimension door, wind walk

STATISTICS

Str 34, Dex 24, Con 28, Int 17, Wis 24, Cha 22
Base Atk +20; CMB +33; CMD 51 (55 vs. trip)
Feats Cleave, Cleaving Finish, Dimensional Agility, Dodge, Great Cleave, Greater Vital Strike, Improved Critical (gore), Improved Vital Strike, Vital Strike, Weapon Focus (gore)
Skills Bluff +26, Intimidate +15, Knowledge (arcana) +14, Knowledge (nature) +23, Knowledge (planes) +18, Perception +30, Stealth +15;
Languages Aklo, Common, Sylvan

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Devastating Antlers (Ex)

The gore attack of the Spirit Elk adds double its Strength bonus to damage and deals triple damage on a critical hit.

Rejuvenation (Su)

After its death, the Spirit Elk ‘rejuvenates’ by taking over a different physical vessel a few weeks later. It almost never seeks revenge against its killers.

Spirit Walk (Su)

A Spirit Elk can use its dimension door spell-like ability as a swift action, just as if it casted it as a quickened spell. When a Spirit Elk uses this ability, it creates a burst of frost from the point of its departure, dealing 10d6 points of cold damage to all creatures within a 30-foot radius and staggering them for 1 round. Succeeding at a DC 29 Fortitude save halves the damage and negates the staggered condition. The save DC is Constitution-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold plains
Organization solitary (unique)
Treasure standard

The Spirit Elk is a creature of myth, and one of uncertain origins. According to various scholars it may be a powerful nature spirit, an incorporeal outsider that’s uniquely hard to put down or even a minor demigod deposed from power. Regardless of its roots, the Spirit Elk has reared its antlered head in most, if not all, cold-dwelling humanoid societies. It is often depicted as a powerful being, most often wandering the most inhospitable stretches of tundra, but sometimes watching over its chosen community and helping it in times of need. In many of those stories, the Spirit Elk inevitably goes mad and starts terrorizing the community, brutally murdering its people one by one, spreading death and frost, slowly killing people off like a savage sadist and leaves the rest trembling in terror and cold. Eventually, a great local force arises. It is either a single heroic figure or a great, brave group. They face the beast and in most of the stories, drive it back or kill it, cementing their place as powerful champions. The stories of lost attempts are sparse and it was only recently that the cause became apparent. If the Spirit Elk is not defeated by those heroes, it depopulates the area overnight, leaving no one alive, and moves to resurface again at a different place and time. Furthermore, the wise men studying the Elk have come to see a pattern in the stories, for the Elk’s madness always coincides with the arrival of heroes. It either starts its terror and the heroes come to fight it, or the heroes gain popularity through their awesome deeds and it soon strikes.

The Spirit Elk is, of course, no elk at all. Most translations from the plethora of local languages from the areas it frequents and the stories are taken from amount to more or less that, so the name stuck. Very rarely, the Spirit Elk takes a different vessel after death. Bears, wolverines and wolves possessed and transformed by the Spirit Elk are a terrifying prospect, but the rarest and perhaps the most devastating form the Spirit Elk can assume is a human. While not as physically strong, the humanoids are uniquely predisposed to both the art of combat and to atrocities, which the Elk uses to its fullest. Only a handful of instances of such a terrifying act are recorded in history, and they are all unconfirmed. It always happens when the Spirit Elk has decided to come back to the same region where it was vanquished before, and it always takes over the vessel of a wild and monstrous barbarian reaver, suitably evil for the new heroes to fight back. Some people and animals in the area of Spirit Elk’s current habitation present with something called the Spirit Elk madness. They become dangerous hermits, often living only to combat dangerous foes nearby with no regard for their own life, but blessed with a small part of the Elk’s incredible strength and vitality, allowing them to pursue challenge with seemingly no pause whatsoever, taking short breaks only to devour raw meat of their foes as fuel. It is unknown if it happens passively or if the Spirit Elk somehow graces the chosen beings through its own power.

In combat, a Spirit Elk is an extremely dangerous foe, although it often gives some leeway to its potential slayers, as long as they give their all. It heals extremely quickly, most of its wounds closing almost instantly, and an overwhelming assault is needed to overcome it, although if it perceives its opponents to fight fairly and with heart, the Spirit Elk never teleports or flies away to let its body completely mend. Its favorite tactic involves teleporting a few dozen feet away using quickened dimension door and charging the vulnerable part of the enemy formation each turn. That makes it very hard to pinpoint, especially with its air walk. Its mobility enables it to attack from a different angle every time. Powerful adversaries might use antimagic fields against the Elk, but it very much doesn’t like that and such opponents may find its appetite for play and heroic combat extinguished, and its antlers fully intent on crushing them this instant.

In its most common vessel, a Spirit Elk is an overgrown, burly, white elk with an antler span of 15 feet and a similar body length. Its animal face is set with two glowing eyes and behaves in a hideously human fashion. It rarely speaks, but has a great penchant for theatrics, even making sure to make a show of its death and demise when defeated.
